judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema's two computed keys both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (z.string().toString() on a Zod schema instance returns Object.prototype.toString's output, and the second computed key overwrites the first), so the sync-mode schema is really z.object({access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional()}) which validates only access_token and strips every other property — the opposite of the commented intent "Allow other properties in the token response". On any host with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every sync-mode parse returns only {access_token}: GoogleCalendarService.ts:96 persists that as the entire credential.key (destroying refresh_token and expiry_date), Office365CalendarService.ts:263 merges it so expiry_date is never updated (stale expiry forces a parent round-trip on every operation), and the app-specific schemas (zoomRefreshedTokenSchema, refreshTokenResponseSchema, salesforceTokenSchema) become dead code, so any parent response with a string access_token is accepted no matter what else it contains or lacks.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines two computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate immediately to string keys (very likely the same literal, e.g. "[object Object]"), so the second overwrites the first and the schema does not actually accept arbitrary keys/expiry fields as intended. Additionally, `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, so in “sync mode” (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the safeParse result will retain essentially only `access_token` (plus the function then mutates in a placeholder `refresh_token`), dropping fields like `expiry_date`/real `refresh_token`. This aligns with the diff’s usage: e.g. Google (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) passes credentials through `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` before persisting, and Office365 merges from the parsed result, so stripped fields would cause stale/missing token data.
